_common.csrf_error_desc: The request was blocked by CSRF protection. If you are accessing Zenith from a non-default URL or reverse proxy, add that origin to the 'csrf_allowed_origins' option in your configuration.

apps.app_name_desc: Application Name, as shown on Moonlight
apps.applications_desc: Applications are refreshed only when Client is restarted
apps.auto_detach: Continue streaming if the application exits quickly
apps.auto_detach_desc: This will attempt to automatically detect launcher-type apps that close quickly after launching another program or instance of themselves. When a launcher-type app is detected, it is treated as a detached app.
apps.cmd_desc: The main application to start. If blank, no application will be started.
apps.cmd_note: If the path to the command executable contains spaces, you must enclose it in double quotes.
apps.cmd_prep_desc: A list of commands to be run before/after this application. If any of the prep-commands fail, starting the application is aborted.
apps.cover_search_hint: Search names should match IGDB naming conventions.
apps.delete_confirm: Are you sure you want to delete {name}?
apps.detached_cmds_desc: A list of commands to be run in the background.
apps.detached_cmds_note: If the path to the command executable contains spaces, you must enclose it in double quotes.
apps.env_client_audio_config: The Audio Configuration requested by the client (2.0/5.1/7.1)
apps.env_client_enable_sops: The client has requested the option to optimize the game for optimal streaming (true/false)
apps.env_client_fps: The FPS requested by the client (int)
apps.env_client_gcmap: The requested gamepad mask, in a bitset/bitfield format (int)
apps.env_client_hdr: HDR is enabled by the client (true/false)
apps.env_client_height: The Height requested by the client (int)
apps.env_client_host_audio: The client has requested host audio (true/false)
apps.env_client_name: The Name of the client assigned during pairing (str)
apps.env_client_width: The Width requested by the client (int)
apps.env_vars_desc: All commands get these environment variables by default:
apps.exit_timeout_desc: Number of seconds to wait for all app processes to gracefully exit when requested to quit. If unset, the default is to wait up to 5 seconds. If set to 0, the app will be immediately terminated.
apps.global_prep_desc: Enable/Disable the execution of Global Prep Commands for this application.
apps.image_desc: Application icon/picture/image path that will be sent to client. Image must be a PNG file. If not set, Zenith will send default box image.
apps.name: Name
apps.no_applications: No applications have been added yet
apps.output_desc: The file where the output of the command is stored, if it is not specified, the output is ignored
apps.run_as_desc: This can be necessary for some applications that require administrator permissions to run properly.
apps.wait_all: Continue streaming until all app processes exit
apps.wait_all_desc: This will continue streaming until all processes started by the app have terminated. When unchecked, streaming will stop when the initial app process exits, even if other app processes are still running.
apps.working_dir_desc: The working directory that should be passed to the process. For example, some applications use the working directory to search for configuration files. If not set, Zenith will default to the parent directory of the command

config.adapter_name_desc_linux_1: Manually specify a GPU to use for capture.
config.adapter_name_desc_linux_2: to find all devices capable of VAAPI
config.adapter_name_desc_linux_3: Replace ``renderD129`` with the device from above to lists the name and capabilities of the device. To be supported by Nova, it needs to have at the very minimum:
config.adapter_name_desc_windows: Manually specify a GPU to use for capture. If unset, the GPU is chosen automatically. We strongly recommend leaving this field blank to use automatic GPU selection! Note: This GPU must have a display connected and powered on. The appropriate values can be found using the following command:
config.address_family_desc: Set the address family used by Nova
config.always_send_scancodes_desc: Sending scancodes enhances compatibility with games and apps but may result in incorrect keyboard input from certain clients that aren't using a US English keyboard layout. Enable if keyboard input is not working at all in certain applications. Disable if keys on the client are generating the wrong input on the host.
config.amd_coder_desc: Allows you to select the entropy encoding to prioritize quality or encoding speed. H.264 only.
config.amd_enforce_hrd_desc: Increases the constraints on rate control to meet HRD model requirements. This greatly reduces bitrate overflows, but may cause encoding artifacts or reduced quality on certain cards.
config.amd_max_au_size_desc: Maximum encoded H.264 or HEVC Access Unit size in bits. Empty or -1 leaves the AMF default. Use only to cap oversized frames that exceed Nova's FEC capacity. The limit depends on packet size and FEC percentage, not bitrate or frame rate. See the documentation for sizing.
config.amd_preanalysis_desc: This enables rate-control preanalysis, which may increase quality at the expense of increased encoding latency.
config.amd_quality_desc: This controls the balance between encoding speed and quality.
config.amd_rc_cbr: cbr -- constant bitrate (recommended if HRD is enabled)
config.amd_rc_desc: This controls the rate control method to ensure we are not exceeding the client bitrate target. 'cqp' is not suitable for bitrate targeting, and other options besides 'vbr_latency' depend on HRD Enforcement to help constrain bitrate overflows.
config.amd_rc_vbr_latency: vbr_latency -- latency constrained variable bitrate (recommended if HRD is disabled; default)
config.amd_usage_desc: This sets the base encoding profile. All options presented below will override a subset of the usage profile, but there are additional hidden settings applied that cannot be configured elsewhere.
config.amd_vbaq_desc: The human visual system is typically less sensitive to artifacts in highly textured areas. In VBAQ mode, pixel variance is used to indicate the complexity of spatial textures, allowing the encoder to allocate more bits to smoother areas. Enabling this feature leads to improvements in subjective visual quality with some content.
config.apply_note: Click 'Apply' to restart Nova and apply changes. This will terminate any running sessions.
config.audio_sink_desc_linux: The name of the audio sink used for Audio Loopback. If you do not specify this variable, pulseaudio will select the default monitor device. You can find the name of the audio sink using either command:
config.audio_sink_desc_macos: The name of the audio sink used for Audio Loopback. Leave this blank to use the built-in system audio capture. Alternatively, specify a virtual device such as Soundflower or BlackHole if you prefer.
config.audio_sink_desc_windows: Manually specify a specific audio device to capture. If unset, the device is chosen automatically. We strongly recommend leaving this field blank to use automatic device selection! If you have multiple audio devices with identical names, you can get the Device ID using the following command:
config.av1_mode_0: Nova will advertise support for AV1 based on encoder capabilities (recommended)
config.av1_mode_1: Nova will not advertise support for AV1
config.av1_mode_2: Nova will advertise support for AV1 Main 8-bit profile
config.av1_mode_3: Nova will advertise support for AV1 Main 8-bit and 10-bit (HDR) profiles
config.av1_mode_desc: Allows the client to request AV1 Main 8-bit or 10-bit video streams. AV1 is more CPU-intensive to encode, so enabling this may reduce performance when using software encoding.
config.back_button_timeout_desc: If the Back/Select button is held down for the specified number of milliseconds, a Home/Guide button press is emulated. If set to a value < 0 (default), holding the Back/Select button will not emulate the Home/Guide button.
config.bind_address_desc: Set an IP address that exists on this host. An IPv4 address works with either address-family mode; an IPv6 address requires dual-stack mode. If left blank, Nova will bind to all available addresses for the configured address family.
config.capture_desc: On automatic mode Nova will use the first one that works. NvFBC requires patched nvidia drivers.
config.cert_desc: The certificate used for the web UI and Moonlight client pairing. For best compatibility, this should have an RSA-2048 public key.
config.channels_desc_1: Nova can allow a single streaming session to be shared with multiple clients simultaneously.
config.channels_desc_2: Some hardware encoders may have limitations that reduce performance with multiple streams.
config.coder_cabac: cabac -- context adaptive binary arithmetic coding - higher quality
config.coder_cavlc: cavlc -- context adaptive variable-length coding - faster decode
config.configuration_desc: Configure Nova's host settings to match your streaming setup.
config.controller_desc: Allows guests to control the host system with a gamepad / controller
config.credentials_file_desc: Store Username/Password separately from Nova's state file.
config.csrf_allowed_origins_desc: Comma-separated list of additional allowed origins for CSRF protection (appended to defaults: localhost variants and web UI port). Only add origins you trust. Each origin must include protocol and host (e.g., https://example.com).
config.dd_config_ensure_only_display: Deactivate other displays and activate only the specified display
config.dd_config_ensure_primary: Activate the display automatically and make it a primary display
config.dd_config_revert_delay_desc: Additional delay in milliseconds to wait before reverting configuration when the app has been closed or the last session terminated. Main purpose is to provide a smoother transition when quickly switching between apps.
config.dd_config_revert_on_disconnect_desc: Revert configuration upon disconnect of all clients instead of app close or last session termination.
config.dd_config_verify_only: Verify that the display is enabled
config.dd_hdr_option_auto: Switch on/off the HDR mode as requested by the client (default)
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_1: Specify remapping entries to change the requested resolution and/or refresh rate to other values.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_2: The list is iterated from top to bottom and the first match is used.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_3: "Requested" fields can be left empty to match any requested value.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_4_final_values_mi: At least one "Final" field must be specified. The unspecified resolution or refresh rate will not be changed.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_4_final_values_no: "Final" field must be specified and cannot be empty.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_5_sops_mixed_only: "Optimize game settings" option must be enabled in the Moonlight client, otherwise entries with any resolution fields specified are skipped.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_5_sops_resolution: "Optimize game settings" option must be enabled in the Moonlight client, otherwise the mapping is skipped.
config.dd_refresh_rate_option_auto: Use FPS value provided by the client (default)
config.dd_resolution_option_auto: Use resolution provided by the client (default)
config.dd_resolution_option_ogs_desc: "Optimize game settings" option must be enabled on the Moonlight client for this to work.
config.dd_wa_hdr_toggle_delay_desc_1: When using virtual display device (VDD) for streaming, it might incorrectly display HDR color. Nova can try to mitigate this issue, by turning HDR off and then on again.
config.dd_wa_hdr_toggle_delay_desc_2: If the value is set to 0, the workaround is disabled (default). If the value is between 0 and 3000 milliseconds, Nova will turn off HDR, wait for the specified amount of time and then turn HDR on again. The recommended delay time is around 500 milliseconds in most cases.
config.dd_wa_hdr_toggle_delay_desc_3: DO NOT use this workaround unless you actually have issues with HDR as it directly impacts stream start time!
config.ds4_back_as_touchpad_click_desc: When using PlayStation-style gamepad emulation, map Back/Select to Touchpad Click
config.virtualhid_randomize_mac_desc: Use a random MAC address for PlayStation-style virtual controllers instead of one based on the controller index. This avoids mixing per-controller settings when controllers are swapped on the client.
config.encoder_desc: Force a specific encoder, otherwise Nova will select the best available option. Note: If you specify a hardware encoder on Windows, it must match the GPU where the display is connected.
config.external_ip_desc: If no external IP address is given, Nova will automatically detect external IP
config.fec_percentage_desc: Percentage of error correcting packets per data packet in each video frame. Higher values can correct for more network packet loss, but at the cost of increasing bandwidth usage.
config.file_apps_desc: The file where current apps of Nova are stored.
config.file_state_desc: The file where current state of Nova is stored
config.gamepad_desc: Choose which type of gamepad to emulate on the host
config.gamepad_driver_desc: Choose which virtual gamepad drivers Nova may use. All Available Drivers prefers Virtual HID Driver when licensed and falls back to ViGEmBus. Virtual HID Driver is an optional paid upgrade. ViGEmBus supports only Xbox 360 and DualShock 4, has limited features, and has reached end of life.
config.global_prep_cmd_desc: Configure a list of commands to be executed before or after running any application. If any of the specified preparation commands fail, the application launch process will be aborted.
config.hevc_mode_0: Nova will advertise support for HEVC based on encoder capabilities (recommended)
config.hevc_mode_1: Nova will not advertise support for HEVC
config.hevc_mode_2: Nova will advertise support for HEVC Main profile
config.hevc_mode_3: Nova will advertise support for HEVC Main and Main10 (HDR) profiles
config.hevc_mode_desc: Allows the client to request HEVC Main or HEVC Main10 video streams. HEVC is more CPU-intensive to encode, so enabling this may reduce performance when using software encoding.
config.high_resolution_scrolling_desc: When enabled, Nova will pass through high resolution scroll events from Moonlight clients. This can be useful to disable for older applications that scroll too fast with high resolution scroll events.
config.install_steam_audio_drivers_desc: If Steam is installed, this will automatically install the Steam Streaming Speakers driver to support 5.1/7.1 surround sound and muting host audio.
config.key_repeat_delay_desc: Control how fast keys will repeat themselves. The initial delay in milliseconds before repeating keys.
config.key_repeat_frequency_desc: How often keys repeat every second. This configurable option supports decimals.
config.key_rightalt_to_key_win: Map Right Alt key to Windows key
config.key_rightalt_to_key_win_desc: It may be possible that you cannot send the Windows Key from Moonlight directly. In those cases it may be useful to make Nova think the Right Alt key is the Windows key
config.keybindings_desc: Remap Windows virtual-key codes received from Moonlight. Each row maps a source code to the code Nova sends to the host. Choose from the complete list of Microsoft-defined virtual-key codes. Incomplete or invalid rows are not saved.
config.keyboard_desc: Allows guests to control the host system with the keyboard
config.lan_encryption_mode_desc: This determines when encryption will be used when streaming over your local network. Encryption can reduce streaming performance, particularly on less powerful hosts and clients.
config.locale_desc: The locale used for Nova's user interface.
config.log_path_desc: The file where the current Nova log is stored. At startup, up to five previous logs are retained with .1 through .5 suffixes.
config.max_bitrate_desc: The maximum bitrate (in Kbps) that Nova will encode the stream at. If set to 0, it will always use the bitrate requested by Moonlight.
config.minimum_fps_target_desc: The lowest effective FPS a stream can reach. A value of 0 is treated as roughly half of the stream's FPS. A setting of 20 is recommended if you stream 24 or 30fps content.
config.max_fps_target_desc: The highest FPS Nova will stream at, regardless of what the client requests. 0 (the default) always honours the client's request. Use this to fix uneven frame pacing when the host's framerate is not a whole multiple of the client's display refresh — 75 FPS into a 60 Hz display, for example, leaves some refreshes showing a stale frame. Note that a clean multiple is usually better than capping: 120 FPS into 60 Hz keeps pacing even while halving frame age, at the cost of extra bandwidth and decoding.
config.min_log_level_desc: The minimum log level printed to standard out
config.min_threads_desc: Increasing the value slightly reduces encoding efficiency, but the tradeoff is usually worth it to gain the use of more CPU cores for encoding. The ideal value is the lowest value that can reliably encode at your desired streaming settings on your hardware.
config.motion_as_ds4: Emulate a PlayStation-style gamepad if the client gamepad reports motion sensors are present
config.motion_as_ds4_desc: If disabled, motion sensors will not be taken into account during gamepad type selection.
config.mouse_desc: Allows guests to control the host system with the mouse
config.native_pen_touch_desc: When enabled, Nova will pass through native pen/touch events from Moonlight clients. This can be useful to disable for older applications without native pen/touch support.
config.clipboard_sync_desc: Share the clipboard with capable Moonlight clients (VoidLink, Foundation-family apps) in both directions: text and images. Currently active on Linux hosts with wl-clipboard (Wayland) or xclip (X11) installed.
config.notify_pre_releases_desc: Whether to be notified of new pre-release versions of Nova
config.nvenc_h264_cavlc: Prefer CAVLC over CABAC in H.264
config.nvenc_h264_cavlc_desc: Simpler form of entropy coding. CAVLC needs around 10% more bitrate for same quality. Only relevant for really old decoding devices.
config.nvenc_latency_over_power: Prefer lower encoding latency over power savings
config.nvenc_latency_over_power_desc: Nova requests maximum GPU clock speed while streaming to reduce encoding latency. Disabling it is not recommended since this can lead to significantly increased encoding latency.
config.nvenc_opengl_vulkan_on_dxgi: Present OpenGL/Vulkan on top of DXGI
config.nvenc_opengl_vulkan_on_dxgi_desc: Nova can't capture fullscreen OpenGL and Vulkan programs at full frame rate unless they present on top of DXGI. This is system-wide setting that is reverted on Nova program exit.
config.nvenc_preset_desc: Higher numbers improve compression (quality at given bitrate) at the cost of increased encoding latency. Recommended to change only when limited by network or decoder, otherwise similar effect can be accomplished by increasing bitrate.
config.nvenc_realtime_hags: Use realtime priority in hardware accelerated gpu scheduling
config.nvenc_realtime_hags_desc: Currently NVIDIA drivers may freeze in encoder when HAGS is enabled, realtime priority is used and VRAM utilization is close to maximum. Disabling this option lowers the priority to high, sidestepping the freeze at the cost of reduced capture performance when the GPU is heavily loaded.
config.nvenc_spatial_aq_desc: Assign higher QP values to flat regions of the video. Recommended to enable when streaming at lower bitrates.
config.nvenc_split_encode_desc: Split the encoding of each video frame over multiple NVENC hardware units. Significantly reduces host processing latency with a marginal compression efficiency penalty. The default option enables SFE if the following conditions are met: there are 2+ NVENC units, the stream is 4K resolution or higher, and the preset is P1-P4. Set this to Enabled to use SFE at lower resolutions or higher presets.
config.nvenc_twopass_desc: Adds preliminary encoding pass. This allows to detect more motion vectors, better distribute bitrate across the frame and more strictly adhere to bitrate limits. Disabling it is not recommended since this can lead to occasional bitrate overshoot and subsequent packet loss.
config.nvenc_vbv_increase_desc: By default Nova uses single-frame VBV/HRD, which means any encoded video frame size is not expected to exceed requested bitrate divided by requested frame rate. Relaxing this restriction can be beneficial and act as low-latency variable bitrate, but may also lead to packet loss if the network doesn't have buffer headroom to handle bitrate spikes. Maximum accepted value is 400, which corresponds to 5x increased encoded video frame upper size limit.
config.origin_web_ui_allowed_desc: The origin of the remote endpoint address that is not denied access to Web UI
config.origin_web_ui_allowed_lan: Only those in LAN may access Web UI
config.origin_web_ui_allowed_pc: Only localhost may access Web UI
config.output_name_desc_macos: During Nova startup, you should see the list of detected displays. Note: You need to use the id value inside the parenthesis. Below is an example; the actual output can be found in the Troubleshooting tab.
config.output_name_desc_unix: During Nova startup, you should see the list of detected displays. Note: It is recommended to use the display's connector name (e.g. DP-0) but depending on the capture backend used other values may be possible (see documentation for details). Below is an example; the actual output can be found in the Troubleshooting tab.
config.output_name_desc_windows: Manually specify a display device id to use for capture. If unset, the primary display is captured. Note: If you specified a GPU above, this display must be connected to that GPU. During Nova startup, you should see the list of detected displays. Below is an example; the actual output can be found in the Troubleshooting tab.
config.packetsize_desc: Limit the packet size to avoid fragmentation on a low MTU link. This helps reduce packet loss and micro-stuttering, while streaming over a layer 2 VPN to clients that cannot configure this value, e.g. Moonlight for Android/iOS. Reduce the bitrate when using low values. Values larger than 1456 require jumbo frames. Range: 0, 200-65535. A value of 0 will disable the limit.
config.ping_timeout_desc: How long to wait in milliseconds for data from moonlight before shutting down the stream
config.pkey_desc: The private key used for the web UI and Moonlight client pairing. For best compatibility, this should be an RSA-2048 private key.
config.port_desc: Set the family of ports used by Nova
config.port_http_port_note: Use this port to connect with Moonlight.
config.port_warning: Exposing the Web UI to the internet is a security risk! Proceed at your own risk!
config.qp_desc: Some devices may not support Constant Bit Rate. For those devices, QP is used instead. Higher value means more compression, but less quality.
config.qsv_slow_hevc_desc: This can enable HEVC encoding on older Intel GPUs, at the cost of higher GPU usage and worse performance.
config.restart_note: Nova is restarting to apply changes.
config.stream_audio_desc: Whether to stream audio or not. Disabling this can be useful for streaming headless displays as second monitors.
config.mic_enabled_desc: Accept microphone audio from connecting clients (Voidlink/Moonlight forks with mic redirection). Creates a virtual "Nova Mic" source in PipeWire that any application can use. Linux only.
config.capture_pacing_desc: How the KMS capture loop schedules frame grabs. Auto paces on display vblank when the client framerate fits the display refresh and falls back to a timer otherwise. Linux only.
config.sunshine_name_desc: The name displayed by Moonlight. If not specified, the PC's hostname is used
config.sw_preset_desc: Optimize the trade-off between encoding speed (encoded frames per second) and compression efficiency (quality per bit in the bitstream). Defaults to superfast.
config.sw_tune_animation: animation -- good for cartoons; uses higher deblocking and more reference frames
config.sw_tune_desc: Tuning options, which are applied after the preset. Defaults to zerolatency.
config.sw_tune_fastdecode: fastdecode -- allows faster decoding by disabling certain filters
config.sw_tune_film: film -- use for high quality movie content; lowers deblocking
config.sw_tune_grain: grain -- preserves the grain structure in old, grainy film material
config.sw_tune_zerolatency: zerolatency -- good for fast encoding and low-latency streaming (default)
config.system_tray_desc: Show icon in system tray and display desktop notifications
config.touchpad_as_ds4: Emulate a PlayStation-style gamepad if the client gamepad reports a touchpad is present
config.touchpad_as_ds4_desc: If disabled, touchpad presence will not be taken into account during gamepad type selection.
config.upnp_desc: Automatically configure port forwarding for streaming over the Internet
config.vaapi_blbrc_desc: Enable block level rate control, which assigns different bitrate block by block. Can be combined with CBR/VBR-type rate control methods on supported encoders.
config.vaapi_quality_desc: Determines encoder tradeoff between quality and speed/power consumption.
config.vaapi_rc_desc: This controls the rate control method to ensure we are not exceeding the client bitrate target. Note that supported rate control methods varies by vendor, and automatic may force-enable strict bitrate enforcement on certain devices.
config.vaapi_strict_rc_buffer: Strictly enforce frame bitrate limits for H.264/HEVC on AMD GPUs
config.vaapi_strict_rc_buffer_desc: Enabling this option can avoid dropped frames over the network during scene changes, but video quality may be reduced during motion.
config.vk_rc_mode_desc: Rate control mode for encoding. Auto lets the driver decide.
config.vk_tune_desc: Low latency modes reduce encoding delay at the cost of quality.
config.virtual_sink_desc: Manually specify a virtual audio device to use. If unset, the device is chosen automatically. We strongly recommend leaving this field blank to use automatic device selection!
config.wan_encryption_mode_desc: This determines when encryption will be used when streaming over the Internet. Encryption can reduce streaming performance, particularly on less powerful hosts and clients.

index.description: Zenith is a self-hosted game stream host for Moonlight.
index.installed_version_not_stable: You are running a pre-release version of Zenith. You may experience bugs or other issues. Please report any issues you encounter. Thank you for helping to make Zenith a better software!
index.new_pre_release: A new Pre-Release Version is Available!
index.new_stable: A new Stable Version is Available!
index.startup_errors: Attention! Zenith detected these errors during startup. We STRONGLY RECOMMEND fixing them before streaming.
index.version_dirty: Thank you for helping to make Zenith a better software!
index.version_latest: You are running the latest version of Zenith
index.virtualhid_development_desc: Thank you for using a development build of Virtual HID Driver. Your testing helps make Virtual HID Driver better!
index.gamepad_driver_choice_desc: Choose whether Zenith may use all available drivers, only Virtual HID Driver, or only ViGEmBus. Virtual HID Driver is an optional paid upgrade. ViGEmBus has limited features and has reached end of life.
index.vigembus_not_installed_desc: ViGEmBus is selected, but it is not installed or running. Install ViGEmBus or choose a different gamepad driver before using gamepad input.
index.vigembus_outdated_desc: ViGEmBus is selected, but the installed version (v{version}) is not supported. Supported versions: {supported_versions}.
index.virtual_input_unavailable_desc: Zenith cannot find a usable virtual gamepad driver. Install and license the optional paid Virtual HID Driver, or install ViGEmBus for limited Xbox 360 and DualShock 4 support. ViGEmBus has reached end of life.
index.virtualhid_license_invalid_desc: The installed Virtual HID Driver does not have a valid paid license, so Zenith cannot use it. Keyboard and mouse input will fall back to SendInput. Get or manage a license, or allow the limited ViGEmBus alternative in Input configuration. ViGEmBus has reached end of life.
index.virtualhid_license_invalid_fallback_desc: The installed Virtual HID Driver does not have a valid paid license. Zenith will fall back to ViGEmBus for Xbox 360 and DualShock 4 gamepads and to SendInput for keyboard and mouse. ViGEmBus has limited features and has reached end of life.
index.virtualhid_optional_desc: Virtual HID Driver is an optional paid upgrade that adds a Raw Input keyboard and mouse, more virtual gamepad types, and modern controller features. Gamepad input is currently disabled.
index.virtualhid_optional_vigembus_desc: ViGEmBus is installed and can provide limited Xbox 360 and DualShock 4 gamepad support. Virtual HID Driver is an optional paid upgrade for more gamepad types, a Raw Input keyboard and mouse, and modern controller features. ViGEmBus has reached end of life.
index.virtualhid_outdated_desc: The installed libvirtualhid driver version (v{version}) is not supported. Supported versions: {supported_versions}.
index.virtualhid_required_desc: Virtual HID Driver is selected, but it is not installed. Install it and activate a paid license, or choose a different gamepad driver in Input configuration.
index.virtualhid_required_title: Virtual HID Driver Is Not Installed

password.new_username_desc: If not specified, the username will not change
password.password_change_desc: Update the username and password used to sign in to the Zenith web UI. You'll need to sign in again after changing them.
password.success_msg: Password has been changed successfully! This page will reload soon, your browser will ask you for the new credentials.

pin.cancel_failure: The pairing request could not be cancelled
pin.load_failure: Pending pairing requests could not be loaded
pin.no_pending_pairings: No devices are waiting to pair
pin.pair_failure: Pairing Failed: Check if the PIN is typed correctly
pin.pair_success: Success! Please check Moonlight to continue
pin.select_pairing_required: Select the device you intend to pair
pin.warning_msg: Make sure you have access to the client you are pairing with. This software can give total control to your computer, so be careful!

resource_card.legal_desc: By continuing to use this software you agree to the terms and conditions in the following documents.

troubleshooting.dd_reset_desc: If Zenith is stuck trying to restore the changed display device settings, you can reset the settings and proceed to restore the display state manually.
troubleshooting.force_close_desc: If Moonlight complains about an app currently running, force closing the app should fix the issue.
troubleshooting.logs_desc: See the logs uploaded by Zenith
troubleshooting.portal_reset_desc: Clear the saved XDG Portal restore token and restart Zenith. You will be prompted to select a display and grant permission again. This will terminate any running sessions.
troubleshooting.portal_reset_error: Failed to clear the saved XDG Portal restore token.
troubleshooting.portal_reset_success: XDG Portal capture was reset. Zenith is restarting.
troubleshooting.restart_sunshine_desc: If Zenith isn't working properly, you can try restarting it. This will terminate any running sessions.
troubleshooting.unpair_desc: Remove your paired devices. Individually unpaired devices with an active session will remain connected, but cannot start or resume a session.
troubleshooting.unpair_single_success: However, the device(s) may still be in an active session. Use the 'Force Close' button above to end any open sessions.
troubleshooting.virtual_gamepad_desc: Virtual HID Driver is an optional paid upgrade for a driver-backed keyboard and mouse plus full virtual gamepad support on Windows. ViGEmBus has limited Xbox 360 and DualShock 4 support and has reached end of life.
troubleshooting.virtual_gamepad_drivers_desc: Installed versions are compared with each project's latest stable GitHub release. Prereleases are ignored.
troubleshooting.virtual_gamepad_licensed_all_desc: Virtual HID Driver is installed, licensed, and ready. Zenith will prefer it for full virtual input support and keep ViGEmBus available as a limited fallback.
troubleshooting.virtual_gamepad_licensed_desc: Virtual HID Driver is installed, licensed, and ready for full virtual input support.
troubleshooting.virtual_gamepad_unset_desc: Choose which Windows virtual gamepad drivers Zenith may use. Virtual HID Driver is an optional paid upgrade. ViGEmBus has limited features and has reached end of life.
troubleshooting.virtual_gamepad_vigembus_desc: Zenith is using ViGEmBus for limited Xbox 360 and DualShock 4 emulation and SendInput for keyboard and mouse. ViGEmBus has reached end of life. Consider upgrading to Virtual HID Driver for broader, actively supported virtual input.
troubleshooting.virtualhid_benefit_features: Supports controller-specific features such as motion, touchpads, LEDs, and adaptive triggers when available.
troubleshooting.virtualhid_benefit_gamepads: Creates Xbox One, Xbox Series, DualSense, Nintendo Switch Pro, and Generic gamepads in addition to Xbox 360 and DualShock 4.
troubleshooting.virtualhid_benefit_mouse: Exposes normal key transitions and relative mouse input through real HID devices so games using Raw Input can receive them.
troubleshooting.virtualhid_benefit_maintained: Virtual HID Driver is actively developed and supported by the LizardByte team. ViGEmBus has reached end of life.
troubleshooting.virtualhid_license_desc: Virtual HID Driver is optional paid software. An active license is required before Zenith can create its gamepads or Raw Input keyboard and mouse. Without a valid license, Zenith uses SendInput for keyboard and mouse. To use the limited ViGEmBus alternative instead, change Windows Gamepad Drivers in Input configuration. ViGEmBus has reached end of life. Activation is handled by the local libvirtualhid service; Zenith does not save your license key.
troubleshooting.virtualhid_license_key_desc: The key is sent only to the local libvirtualhid service and is cleared from this page after successful activation.
troubleshooting.virtualhid_license_machine_activated_des: Zenith can create Virtual HID Driver gamepads and a Raw Input keyboard and mouse while this license remains valid.
troubleshooting.virtualhid_license_unavailable: The local libvirtualhid license service is unavailable. Verify that the driver package and broker service are installed and running.

apps.title: Applications
apps.subtitle: Apps clients can start. Clients see changes the next time they refresh their app list.
apps.load_failed_desc: The host didn’t return the app list. Check that Nova is running, then try again.
apps.empty_desc: Add a game, launcher or desktop session so clients can start it.
apps.no_results_desc: Try a different name or command.
apps.delete_desc: {name} is removed from the app list. Its cover and any files it uses stay on this PC.
apps.close_desc: The app that’s streaming now is closed, and connected clients return to their app list.
apps.close_failed: Couldn’t close the app. Try again.
apps.save_failed: The host didn’t accept the change. Check the fields and try again.
apps.error_name_required: Enter a name. Clients show it in their app list.
apps.error_exit_timeout: Enter a whole number of seconds, 0 or more.
apps.field_command_hint: The program to start. Leave empty to stream the desktop. Put quotes around paths that contain spaces.
apps.field_working_dir_hint: Folder the command starts in. Some games look for their files here.
apps.field_image_hint: PNG file sent to clients. Leave empty to use the default box art.
apps.prep_desc: Commands that run before the app starts and after it closes. If a “before” command fails, the app doesn’t start.
apps.field_global_prep_hint: Also run the prep commands set in Settings for every app.
apps.detached_desc: Started alongside the app and left running. Nova doesn’t wait for them or close them.
apps.field_auto_detach: Keep streaming if the app exits right away
apps.field_auto_detach_hint: For launchers that start the real game and close. Nova keeps the stream open instead of ending it.
apps.field_wait_all: Wait for all of the app’s processes
apps.field_wait_all_hint: Keep streaming until every process the app started has exited, not just the first one.
apps.field_elevated_hint: Some apps need administrator rights to run correctly.
apps.field_exit_timeout_hint: How long to wait for the app to close when asked to quit, before it’s forced. Leave empty for 5 seconds; 0 closes it at once.
apps.field_output_hint: Where to save the command’s output. Leave empty to discard it.
apps.env_desc: Every command gets these variables, so scripts can match the client’s display.
apps.env_example: Example: set the resolution to the client’s
apps.discard_desc: The changes you made to this application aren’t saved yet.
apps.browse_not_found: That folder doesn’t exist or can’t be opened.
apps.cover_desc: Covers come from IGDB. Search with the game’s official name.
apps.cover_search_failed: Couldn’t search for covers. Check the internet connection and try again.
apps.cover_save_failed: Couldn’t save that cover on the host. Try another one.
apps.cover_none_desc: Try the full official title, or fewer words.
apps.not_found: That application doesn’t exist any more. It may have been deleted.
